topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture’s aims and connects its focus on cancer evolution to earlier lectures.

topics.label: Mutation-driven clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how successive mutations confer selective advantages that allow fitter clones to expand.

topics.label: Epigenetic disruption as a route to cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines whether altered transcriptional states can drive tumor development without mutational change.

topics.label: Stemness, tumor hierarchy and the cell of origin
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how a cell’s position in a differentiation hierarchy influences its capacity to initiate and propagate cancer.

topics.label: Inflammation-induced stemness in cancer promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how inflammatory microenvironments enable mutation-bearing cells to develop tumors by inducing stem-like properties.

topics.label: Microenvironmental support of established tumors
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines established tumors’ dependence on supportive stromal cells as a vulnerability that therapy could target.

topics.label: Investigating cancer evolution with single-cell and spatial methods
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tissue-based molecular methods reveal tumor cell states and interactions within their microenvironment.

topics.label: Converging conditions for malignant evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic integrates the lecture’s mechanisms into an account of how malignant growth depends on the right cellular conditions arising together, including during childhood development.

topics.label: Lecture close and next lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic ends the lecture and announces the forthcoming discussion of cancer therapy.
